AboutSection.title: A community for AI enthusiasts
AboutSection.description: The Artificial Intelligence Community (AIC) was founded in 2024 to create a scientific space for students interested in AI, under the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence.
AboutSection.body: From educational workshops and scientific conferences to industry collaboration and research projects, members grow in a dynamic and creative environment.

AboutPage.title: About AIC
AboutPage.heroB: An association for learning, building projects and teaching the next person.
AboutPage.originLead: From one simple need to an association that is still being built.
AboutPage.audienceLead: Whichever of the three you are, the first step is easier here.
AboutPage.headline: Where we learn AI and technology, build with it, and teach it to each other
AboutPage.lede: Since 2024, the Artificial Intelligence Community has brought students together under the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence. AI is our core, but not our limit: web, security, networks, and IoT are part of the path too.

areas.title: Machine and deep learning
areas.desc: From regression to neural networks in PyTorch; the base of most AI work.

areas.title: Natural language processing
areas.desc: Machines that read and write text, from tokenizers to transformers.

areas.title: Computer vision
areas.desc: Teaching computers to see: detection, segmentation, and understanding images and video.

areas.title: Web development
areas.desc: Front end and back end; building real products that put ideas and models in users' hands.

areas.title: Security and networks
areas.desc: Networks, security, and infrastructure; knowing how what we build stays safe and reliable.

areas.title: IoT and robotics
areas.desc: Where software meets hardware and the physical world: sensors, control, and smart systems.

AboutPage.manifesto: We believe you understand AI, and any other technology, by building it. That is why we step out of the classroom, build projects together, and teach what we learn to the next person.

principles.title: Build to understand
principles.body: An idea gets clearer when we implement it, test it, and see where it fails.

principles.title: Move the project together
principles.body: Shared work gives us a reason to ask, explain, and complete each other’s understanding.

principles.title: Teach the next person
principles.body: What we learn does not stop with us. We pass it on in a way the next student can use.

AboutPage.originTitle: A young association, still writing its path
origin: The Artificial Intelligence Association was founded in 2024 under the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence.
Students needed a place to build, test, and talk about AI and the technologies around it outside class.
That continues through workshops, conferences, student contests, industry and lab visits, and research projects. The story is still being written.
AboutPage.pillarsTitle: What a semester here feels like
AboutPage.pillarsDescription: Each path is another way out of the classroom, from solving a problem together to seeing real work up close.

semester.title: Contest
semester.body: We start with a clear problem and build and test a solution as a team. A contest is where ideas, shared work, and the result all get a turn.

semester.title: Conference
semester.body: We hear new topics, viewpoints, and directions up close. Asking questions makes both the research and the applications easier to see.

semester.title: Workshop
semester.body: Machine learning, language, vision, and deep learning are practiced, not only described. We build something, find the failure, and learn why it works.

semester.title: Visit
semester.body: Industry and lab visits show how a team works on a real problem. The gap between coursework, research, and implementation gets concrete.

semesterNext.title: The next step is yours
semesterNext.body: The next semester is not written yet. See what is on the calendar and take your first step.

AboutPage.audienceTitle: If this is you, there is a place here

audience.title: You are just starting
audience.body: If you are still finding a way into AI, this is a place to ask, try things, and pick a starting point.

audience.title: You want to build
audience.body: If you want to turn what you know into an exercise, a contest entry, or a research project, you can work on it with other students.

audience.title: You want to teach
audience.body: If you are ready to pass on what you know, or to carry part of an activity, there is room for you to take it on.

items.title: Python foundations for AI
items.speaker: Ali Heydari
items.desc: A hands-on primer on the Python tooling used across every AIC workshop — NumPy, pandas, and notebooks — for members starting from zero.

items.title: AIC departments kickoff
items.desc: New semester, new departments. Meet the working groups behind AIC's research and events, and find where your skills fit best.

items.title: Deep learning with PyTorch
items.speaker: Negar Salehi
items.desc: Build and train a neural network from scratch in PyTorch, then walk through debugging, tuning, and evaluating it on real data.

items.title: Generative AI week
items.speaker: AIC instructor team
items.desc: A week of talks and build sessions on generative text, image, and audio models, closing with a showcase of member-built projects.

items.title: NLP with transformers
items.speaker: Maryam Karimi
items.desc: From tokenizers to fine-tuning — a practical tour of transformer-based models for text classification and generation.

items.title: AIC AI hackathon
items.desc: Two days, small teams, one working AI prototype. Mentors are on hand throughout, with prizes for the top three teams.

items.title: Industry talk: careers in AI
items.speaker: Kaveh Rostami
items.desc: An industry guest on breaking into an applied-AI career: what teams actually hire for, and how to build a portfolio that shows it.

items.title: Intelligent robotics workshop
items.speaker: Behnam Taheri
items.desc: Programme a small robot's control loop and train a simple reinforcement-learning agent to guide it through a simulated course.

ContactPage.faqLead: Most of what you want to ask is answered here.

faq.q: How do I join the association?
faq.a: Choose "Membership request" on this page and write your message. The team reads it and follows up by email or phone.

faq.q: Can I help run a workshop or an industry visit?
faq.a: Yes. Choose "Partnership" and describe the collaboration: a workshop, an industry visit or a research project.

faq.q: Where do I go to visit in person?
faq.a: Faculty of Artificial Intelligence, Education Building No. 2; Saturday to Wednesday 8:00–18:00, Thursday and Friday 10:00–16:00. If you want a focused conversation, write first so we can coordinate.

faq.q: Where do I hear about events and workshops?
faq.a: Events and activities are published on this site; you can also follow the association on Instagram, LinkedIn and Telegram.

faq.q: What do I need to write a message?
faq.a: A name, an email, a phone number and the message itself. We ask for a phone number so we can coordinate faster when needed.
